profile.campus: Allen, Collin County, Texas (CyrusOne DFW3-DFW5 campus)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, the Allen, Texas (DFW3-DFW5) campus sits at 2300 Chelsea Boulevard, Allen, TX 75013, publishing 976,000 sq ft and 77 MW of total IT capacity across three buildings.

CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten; the company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it for approximately $15 billion. The Dallas-Fort Worth metro is anchored by CyrusOne's Carrollton (DFW1) facility, which Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry describes the company itself calling the largest data center in Texas when it opened in 2012, and today spans additional DFW-numbered buildings in Allen and Lewisville; Texas's absence of a state corporate income tax and its position as a major interstate fiber crossroads have helped make the state, alongside Northern Virginia, one of CyrusOne's largest concentrations of US facilities.

In 2016, CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease, a transaction illustrating the sale-leaseback and anchor-tenant financing structures common among large colocation operators. Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued to expand its US footprint, including the January 2025 groundbreaking of a new fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6) representing roughly $1 billion in cumulative San Antonio capital investment per the company's own materials, indicating continued growth investment in Texas markets under private ownership rather than a slowdown following the take-private transaction.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne Allen campus sits near Dallas Fort Worth and reports 77 MW of IT load across three connected facilities. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this translates roughly to 1,900 racks. The campus holds FISMA and HIPAA certifications, qualifying it to host federal workloads and regulated healthcare data.

Allen ranks second among the 18 Texas facilities that publish power consumption, representing 16 percent of the state's 468 MW of disclosed data center IT capacity. Texas has 133 mapped data center locations overall, most of which do not publish figures, so actual deployed capacity exceeds published capacity by an unknown margin.

The facility occupies 976,000 square feet across three buildings, a footprint large enough to support future expansion. Whether the campus can grow depends on grid availability at the Allen location, which is not published. CyrusOne operates multiple facilities across Texas, anchored by an earlier phase in the Dallas Fort Worth cluster itself, but individual site power constraints and grid interconnection status remain opaque to outside observers.
